researchQuestion: Does GPT-5.4 Mini generalize as an evidence-sufficiency assessor on newly curated question-evidence packets that were not used in the v1 error analysis?
hypothesis: Because the v1 disagreements were caused by strict canonical-chunk labels, a semantic assessor will outperform the score-and-language gate on human-reviewed packets containing valid alternative evidence while maintaining at most one false positive among twelve insufficient packets.
singleChangedVariable: Deterministic score-and-language sufficiency assessment versus GPT-5.4 Mini semantic assessment on the same frozen evidence packets.

benchmark.overlapPolicy: No state id or complete question-evidence packet may occur in agentic-semantic-assessor-v1. Golden-set test cases and the locked 24-case test split are excluded.
benchmark.referencePolicy: A blinded human review of all 24 packets is frozen before either assessor is executed. Intended construction labels are not treated as gold labels.

selectionRule.decision: Qualify the semantic assessor for one new end-to-end validation experiment only if every frozen quality and operational guardrail passes. This benchmark cannot enable production directly.

executionOrder: Complete blinded human review of every packet.
Freeze the human-reference CSV and its SHA-256.
Execute deterministic and semantic assessors once without prompt changes.
Publish all predictions, metrics, costs, and disagreements.
limitations: Twenty-four packets support a bounded component check, not a high-powered population estimate.
Questions and evidence are curated from the existing corpus and therefore measure in-domain generalization.
The primary reviewer is also the thesis author; this does not estimate inter-rater reliability.
